# HD4 -- Agent API

> HD4 is a four-channel video switcher with an audio mixer, in the browser.
> Each channel shows a camera, a video or image file, a pattern or fill from
> the source library, or a Noisemaker shader program. A program is Noisemaker
> DSL text that compiles to a render graph. An agent can join the person's own
> open HD4 over Seance, the Noise Factor collaboration service, and then set
> channel programs, switch and transition between channels, composite, apply
> output effects, ride the audio mixer, use memory slots, and look at any
> monitor. An agent that drives its own browser can use the in-page
> `window.HD4Agent` API instead. This file is the contract for software agents
> that control HD4.

The full contract adds a reference for every command and its arguments:
https://hd4.noisefactor.io/llms-full.txt

The DSL itself (syntax, effects, parameters, surfaces) is specified by the
Noisemaker contract: https://noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt

For the roles and control paths of the other Noise Factor visual products,
including Timeline's project-folder CLI and Layers' separate document, read
the product map at https://noisedeck.app/llms-full.txt.

## Connect to the person's HD4

Use this route when you can run shell commands. It works with the HD4 the
person already has open: their channels, their monitors, their mix.

1. Ask the person to open https://hd4.noisefactor.io, choose **Connect
   agent…** at the end of the Program group in any channel's source picker,
   click **Go Online**, then **Copy Prompt**, and paste the prompt to you. The
   prompt names this file and the session link. (Without that dialog: **live
   collab...** in the same place, **Take Online**, then send the link or the
   six-character code.)
2. Get the agent tool. It needs Node 22.4 or later and nothing else:
   `curl -fsSLO https://noisedeck.app/agent/seance-agent.mjs`
3. Join: `node seance-agent.mjs join <link-or-code>`. It prints the session
   name (`hd4`), the open app tabs and the four channel documents. A
   background process keeps the session joined between commands.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node seance-agent.mjs commands` | Lists HD4's commands and their arguments. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs look [--size N] [--format png\|jpg] [--out FILE]` | Saves an image of the program output. Its path is `result.envelope.result.image.path`; open the file with your image tool. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs look --args '{"source":2}'` | Saves an image of channel 2 (`"preview"` is the PVW channel). |
| `node seance-agent.mjs set <file> --args '{"channel":2}'` | Runs a program on channel 2 (setProgram). Without `--args` it goes to the PVW channel. `-` reads standard input. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs validate <file>` | Checks a program without running it. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs call take '{"channel":2}'` | Runs any command with JSON arguments. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs call getProgram '{"channel":2}'` | Prints one channel's program in an envelope. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs program --doc channel:2 [--json]` | Prints channel 2's document text. Without `--doc` it prints channel 1. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs wait --doc channel:2 [--since REV] [--timeout S]` | Waits for the person to change channel 2's program, then prints it. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs image-put <file>` | Adds a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file to the session. `result.ref` is its `image:<id>`. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs transfer <from> <to> --to-args '{"channel":2}'` | Copies a program and its images from one joined session to another, here to HD4 channel 2. With HD4 as the source, `--from-args '{"channel":2}'` picks the channel. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs leave` / `stop` | Leaves the session / stops the background process. |

Every command prints JSON, except `program` and `commands`, which print text
(`--json` gives JSON). The exit code is 0 for
success, 1 when HD4 refused the command (read `result.envelope.error.code`),
and 2 when the tool could not run it (read `error.code`; the codes are listed
below). `node seance-agent.mjs help` lists every option.

How it works, so you can explain it to the person:

- The tool joins the session as an anonymous participant, which the person
  sees join. It runs commands in the HD4 tab that took the channels online,
  through the session, through the same code as the person's own controls:
  the panels and the readout show each change. No other tab answers, even one
  that becomes the session's owner after the person's tab leaves. The
  person's tab answers again after they reload it.
- The session holds one document per channel, `channel:1` to `channel:4`. A
  channel that runs a shader program holds its program text. A channel that
  shows a camera, a video or an image holds empty text: cameras, video and
  image files never leave the person's computer. Text written into a
  document reaches only a channel that shows a program; `setProgram` is how
  an agent puts a program on any channel.
- Everyone in the session receives every answer, and anyone who can edit the
  session can send commands to that tab. So what the person keeps in this
  browser is not reachable through a session: the memory slots (`listMemory`,
  `saveMemory`, `recallMemory`), the settings and USER buttons (`getSettings`,
  `setSettings`, `setUserButton`), stills (`captureStill`, and `still` as a
  source in `setSource` or `setKey`) and device names (`listDevices`) answer
  `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`. So do the commands that
  need the person at the browser: camera or microphone permission
  (`setCameraSource`, `setAudioInput`), a recording download (`setRecording`)
  and a pop-up window (`openViewport`). `commands` marks them. Suggest that the
  person goes offline when you are done: **stop live collab** in a channel's
  source picker opens the session dialog, which has **Go Offline**.
- `look` asks the person's tab for an image of a monitor. The tab adds the
  image to the session as its own bytes, and the tool saves it as a file.
  `look` works only while every channel shows a program (a shader program or
  a pattern or fill from the source library) and FREEZE is off. While a
  channel shows a camera, a video, an image or a still, or still shows the
  last frame of one while its new program starts, or the KEY shows the still,
  `look` answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`: those stay on the person's computer.
  `look` at the program output also answers it while the person's HD4 tab is
  hidden, because a hidden tab does not draw the output.
  HD4 starts with a camera on channel 1 and the test card on channel 2, so ask
  the person to put programs or library sources on them first. Through a
  session, `getProgram` answers with the text the session holds, and a local
  source goes by its kind, never by its file name.
- A session holds at most 32 images, and the person's own images need room
  too. The tab takes at most 16 images in ten minutes; past that, `look`
  answers `IMAGE_LIMIT` with `details.retryAfter` in seconds. Look when the
  mix has changed, not in a loop.

Work with several apps at once: join each app's session (each gets its own
name, such as `hd4`, `noisedeck` or `visualize`), then name the session in
each command: `set hd4 prog.dsl --args '{"channel":3}'`, `look noisedeck`,
`transfer noisedeck hd4 --to-args '{"channel":3}'`. A transfer copies the
program's images as bytes, so `media(url: "image:<sha256>")` references keep
working in HD4. HD4 checks the program and refuses one that it cannot compile.
An HD4 session holds HD4 documents only: other apps cannot join it, and HD4
joins only sessions that HD4 took online. Programs move between apps through
the agent tool.

Agent tool errors (exit code 2, `error.code`):

- `NO_SESSION`: no session is joined, or more than one and none was named.
- `UNKNOWN_SESSION`, `SESSION_LOCKED`, `REFUSED`: the session code is wrong or
  expired, the session is locked, or the session refused the join.
- `NO_APP_TAB`: the tab that took the session online did not answer. Ask the
  person to keep it open, or to go online again and send the new code.
- `TIMEOUT`: the tab did not answer in time. Check `status`, then try again.
- `READONLY`: the session lets this agent only read the program text:
  `program`, `wait` and `status` work, and every app command, `commands` and
  `look` included, is refused. Ask the person to allow guests to edit.
- `SESSION_CLOSED`, `SESSION_REFUSED`: the connection closed, or the session
  server refused a request (the message says why).
- `IMAGE_FAILED`, `NO_DOCUMENT`, `USAGE`, `INVALID_JSON`: an image transfer
  failed, a document is missing, or the command line was wrong.
- `CONNECT_FAILED`, `RATE_LIMITED`: `join` could not reach the session server,
  or the server is limiting joins from this address. Wait a minute, then join
  again.
- `INVALID_IMAGE`, `BAD_RESPONSE`: an image id is malformed, or the app sent
  an answer that the tool could not read.
- `DAEMON_FAILED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`: the tool's background process did not
  start, or the tool failed. If it happens again, run `stop` and join again.
- A file that the tool cannot read gives the system's code, such as `ENOENT`.

## Control HD4 in a browser you drive

Use this route when you control a browser yourself. Open
https://hd4.noisefactor.io. Use the first route your browser tool supports:

1. WebMCP: discover the page tools named `hd4_getState`, `hd4_setProgram`,
   and so on. Each tool has the argument schema below. These call the same API
   and return its envelope as text. `getThumbnail` also returns an image
   content block, without duplicating its bytes in text. If your harness
   serializes the whole tool result, parse it, display the image through your
   image tool, and print only the text block. Do not print image bytes.
2. Page JavaScript: call `window.HD4Agent` directly. Wait until the object and
   method exist. Every command waits for startup automatically; explicitly
   awaiting `ready` also works. Return the fields you need, not the whole API
   object.

```js
const env = await window.HD4Agent.getProgram({ channel: 3 })
return env.result.dsl
```

Both routes use the same serialized commands and validation. WebMCP
availability depends on the browser. If discovery returns no tools, use page
JavaScript. Do not try to bypass a browser tool's read-only JavaScript policy.
A tool that only fetches HTML cannot run HD4. A browser is required.
Channel 1 starts on the default camera, so the browser can ask for camera
permission when HD4 opens.

---

## Channels, preview and program

- Channels are numbered 1 to 4. `state.program.live` is the channel on
  program (PGM), the output. `state.program.preview` is the channel queued on
  preview (PVW).
- `setProgram`, `getProgram`, `setSource` and `setCameraSource` act on the PVW
  channel when you omit `channel`, like the person's Cmd/Ctrl+V paste. Check a
  new program on preview, then `take` it to program.
- `take` without `channel` takes the PVW channel, and the outgoing program
  returns to PVW. `take({ channel: 3 })` takes channel 3 and leaves PVW alone.
  `transition: "auto"` (the default) uses the selected transition type and
  time; `transition: "cut"` switches at once, also during a transition. An
  `auto` take is refused while a transition runs; read
  `state.program.transitioning`.
- `setSource` shows a pattern or fill from the source library (`Color Bars`,
  `Checkerboard`, `Grid`, `UV Map`, `Dot Grid`, `Color Grid`, `Black`,
  `White`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Amber`) or `still`, the still captured in
  this page (with the STILL button or `captureStill`).
- `getThumbnail` shows the program output by default. `source: "preview"`
  shows the PVW channel, and `source: 1` to `4` shows that channel.

## Write a program

1. Find effects with `searchEffects`. Read their parameters with `getEffectDefinition`.
2. Write the program. Copy each parameter name from `getEffectDefinition`. Do not guess names.
   `choices` lists accepted values. For a `member` parameter, insert its value as a DSL
   member expression, such as `palette.hypercolor`, without quotes.
3. Check it with `validateProgram`. Fix every diagnostic with severity `error`.
4. Run it with `setProgram`. Look at the channel with `getThumbnail`
   (`source` set to the channel), then `take` it to program.
5. To change one parameter, edit its argument in the program text and run the
   program again.

```js
const A = window.HD4Agent
const dsl = [
    'search synth, mixer',
    'noise(ridges: true).write(o0)',
    'gradient().blendMode(tex: read(o0), mode: overlay, mix: 25).write(o1)',
    'render(o1)',
].join('\n')
const check = await A.validateProgram({ dsl })
if (!check.result.valid) return check.result.diagnostics
const run = await A.setProgram({ dsl, channel: 2 })
if (!run.ok) return run.error
const taken = await A.take({ channel: 2 })
return taken.result
```

DSL rules that agents most often get wrong:

- The first line `search ns1, ns2` sets the namespaces that effect names resolve in, in order.
  The same function name can mean different effects in different namespaces,
  with different parameters.
- Every chain ends with `.write(oN)`. The program ends with `render(oN)`.
- Read another surface with `read(oN)`, for example `tex: read(o0)`.
- Noisemaker 1.0.289 retired all old parameter aliases. Older examples use names
  such as `mixAmt`, `noiseType` or `loopAmp`. Those now fail with
  `S001 Unknown argument`. `getEffectDefinition` gives the current names.
- An image is `media(url: "image:<sha256>")`, the SHA-256 of the image's
  bytes. HD4 takes the image from the Seance session the tab is in (add one
  with the agent tool's `image-put`), as bytes; an image never travels as
  text (`IMAGE_AS_TEXT`), and a session program cannot name media by an
  outside link (`OUTSIDE_LINK`). Offline, or when the session lacks the image, the
  program still runs, its media step stays empty, and the envelope carries an
  `IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE` warning.

## Run the mix

- `setTransition`: type `cut`, `mix` or `wipe`, time 0 to 4 seconds, fade
  curve, MIX blend mode.
- `setComposition`: `off`, `pinp`, `split` or `quad`, with the PinP inset
  (source, size, shape, aspect, border, position, crop) and the SPLIT
  parameters. `setKey`: the chroma or luma KEY overlay over the program.
- `setOutput`: FREEZE, OUTPUT FADE (fade to black) and the output VFX filter.
  `captureStill` grabs the program as a still (in a browser you drive).
- `setAuto`: beat-synced auto-switching (scan, random or follows-audio), bars
  per switch, tempo, and SYNC to the audio.
- `setAudioChannel` and `setAudioMain`: faders, mute, solo, each channel's
  audio source and processing, the main bus, monitoring and the recording
  source. `getControls({ section: "audio" })` reads them all.
- In a browser you drive: `listMemory`, `saveMemory` and `recallMemory` use the
  eight memory slots with the full mixer state (a save replaces what the slot
  held); `getSettings` and `setSettings` read and set the output resolution,
  OUTPUT FADE time, beat sensitivity and theme; `setUserButton` assigns the
  USER buttons. Through a session, ask the person to use MEM, the settings
  drawer and the USER buttons.
- Omitted fields keep their value in every `set...` command.

What only the person can do: choose a video or image file (a file picker; an
agent shows images through `media(url: "image:<sha256>")` programs instead),
paste from the clipboard (`setProgram` does the same), pair Noisedeck Sync
output (its dialog), and set up MIDI (it needs their controller). The
reference marks every command that a session cannot run.

---

## Keep results small

Your browser tool sends each script result back to you.
A large result uses a large part of your context.

- Return only the fields that you need from each script.
- Every envelope includes `state`. Remove it when you do not need it.
- Direct JavaScript `getThumbnail` returns base64 image data. Keep `maxDimension` small.
  WebMCP returns the image as its own content block and omits its bytes from text.
- The agent tool saves images as files and prints only their paths. Open a file
  with your image tool; do not print its bytes.
- The agent tool removes `state` from envelopes. Add `--state` to keep it.
- `getControls` returns one section at a time. Ask only for the section you need.

---

## The envelope

Every command response, success or failure, has this shape:

```js
// success
{ ok: true, command: "setProgram", apiVersion: "1.0", result: { /* command-specific */ }, state: { /* snapshot */ } }

// failure
{
    ok: false,
    command: "setProgram",
    apiVersion: "1.0",
    error: { code: "INVALID_PROGRAM", message: "...", details: { diagnostics: [ /* ... */ ] } },
    state: { /* snapshot */ }
}
```

A success can carry `warnings`, a list of `{ code, message, ... }`. The one
warning is `IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE` (with `imageIds`): the program runs, but the
images it names are not in the session or the page.

Commands run one at a time, in the order you call them.
You can omit the argument object: `getState()` is the same as `getState({})`.
Every command rejects an argument that it does not declare, so a command
with no arguments accepts only `{}`.

---

## State snapshot

```
state: {
    schemaVersion,
    program:     { live, preview, transitioning },   // live: the PGM channel; preview: the PVW channel
    channels:    [ { channel, source, name, chars, running } ],
                                         // source: "shader", "camera", "video", "image" or "none"
                                         // chars: program length; running: the program compiled and runs
    transition:  { type, time, curve, blend },
    composition: { mode, key },          // mode: "off", "pinp", "split" or "quad"; key: the KEY overlay is on
    output:      { freeze, fade, vfx, recording, width, height },
                                         // fade: fading to or holding black; width, height: the program output
    auto:        { on, mode, bars, bpm },
    online:      { status, session }     // status: "offline", "connecting", "online" or "readonly"
}
```

---

## Diagnostics

`validateProgram` and a failed `setProgram` return compiler diagnostics:

```js
{ code: "S001", severity: "error", message: "Unknown argument 'mixAmt' for blendMode()", location?: { line, column } }
```

A syntax error has code `SYNTAX`. Diagnostics with severity `warning` do not stop a program.

---

## Error codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_ARGS_TYPE` | wrong argument type |
| `INVALID_ARGS_REQUIRED` | missing required argument |
| `INVALID_ARGS_RANGE` | number or string length out of range |
| `INVALID_ARGS_ENUM` | value not in the allowed list |
| `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN` | an argument that the command does not declare |
| `INVALID_PROGRAM` | the program does not compile. `details.diagnostics` lists the errors. Nothing changed |
| `COMPILE_FAILED` | the channel could not show the program or source. It shows its previous source again |
| `CONFLICT_CHANNEL_CHANGED` | another change took the channel while the new source started. The channel shows that change |
| `CONFLICT_TRANSITION_RUNNING` | an `auto` take while a transition runs. Nothing changed |
| `NOT_FOUND_EFFECT` | unknown effect id |
| `NOT_FOUND_STILL` | `setSource` with `still` before any still was captured |
| `NOT_FOUND_MEMORY` | `recallMemory` on an empty slot |
| `NOT_FOUND_COMMAND` | the session asked for a command that HD4 does not have |
| `EFFECT_LOAD_FAILED` | an effect could not load from the CDN |
| `DEVICE_FAILED` | the camera did not start (no camera, or no permission). The channel shows its previous source again |
| `MEMORY_SAVE_FAILED` | the browser refused to store the memory slot. The slot keeps what it held |
| `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` | through a session: the command needs the person at the browser, reads or changes what this browser keeps, or would show a camera, a video, an image file or a still |
| `IMAGE_LIMIT` | the tab already took 16 images in ten minutes. `details.retryAfter` is in seconds |
| `IMAGE_AS_TEXT` | a session request or answer would carry an image as base64 text. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `OUTSIDE_LINK` | a session request names media by an outside link. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `IMAGE_UPLOAD_FAILED` | the tab could not add an image to the session (the session holds up to 32 images) |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | unexpected failure |

---

## Command reference

HD4 has 31 commands. Call a command as `await window.HD4Agent.<name>(args)`,
as the WebMCP tool `hd4_<name>`, or through a Seance session with the agent tool.
Every command rejects an argument that it does not declare, with `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN`.

### Read state

#### `getState`

Returns the state snapshot. Every envelope already includes it in `state`.

Returns: the snapshot.

Arguments: none.

#### `getProgram`

Returns the program text of one channel and whether it is the program that runs. A channel that shows a camera, a video, an image or nothing has no program text. Through a Seance session it is the text the session holds for the channel. `channel` defaults to the PVW channel.

Returns: `{ channel, source, dsl, running }`, where `source` is `shader`, `camera`, `video`, `image` or `none`.

Arguments:

- `channel`: integer, from 1 to 4

#### `getControls`

Returns every parameter of one section of the live mixer: `channels` (sources, fit, AUTO rotation, whether a still was captured), `composition` (PinP, SPLIT and KEY parameters), `audio` (strips, main bus, monitor, record source) or `auto` (auto-switching and tempo).

Returns: `{ section, ... }` with the section's values.

Arguments:

- `section` (required): string, one of `channels`, `composition`, `audio`, `auto`

### Programs

#### `validateProgram`

Compiles `dsl` without applying it.

Returns: `{ valid, diagnostics }`.

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character, at most 65536 characters

#### `setProgram`

Compiles `dsl` and makes it the shader source of one channel, like a pasted program. `channel` defaults to the PVW channel, so a new program can be checked on preview before a take. A program that does not compile changes nothing and fails with INVALID_PROGRAM. A channel that showed a camera, a video or an image stops it.

Returns: `{ applied: true, channel, diagnostics }` (warnings only).

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character, at most 65536 characters
- `channel`: integer, from 1 to 4

### Effects

#### `searchEffects`

Lists effects whose id, description or tags contain `query`. `namespace` keeps one namespace.

Returns: `{ total, effects: [{ effectId, namespace, name, description, tags }] }`.

Arguments:

- `query`: string
- `namespace`: string
- `limit`: integer, from 1 to 500, default `50`

#### `getEffectDefinition`

Returns the DSL function name and the parameters of one effect.

Returns: `{ effectId, func, namespace, description, params: [{ name, type, default, min?, max?, enum?, choices?, label? }] }`.

Arguments:

- `effectId` (required): string, at least 1 character

### Channels

#### `setSource`

Shows a pattern or a fill from the source library on a channel, or `still`, the still captured in this page (see captureStill; not through a Seance session). `channel` defaults to the PVW channel.

Returns: `{ channel, source, name }`.

Arguments:

- `channel`: integer, from 1 to 4
- `source` (required): string, one of `Color Bars`, `Checkerboard`, `Grid`, `UV Map`, `Dot Grid`, `Color Grid`, `Black`, `White`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Amber`, `still`

#### `setChannelOptions`

Sets how a camera, video or image fills the channel (`cover` crops, `contain` scales) and whether the channel takes part in the AUTO rotation.

Returns: `{ channel, fit, autoInclude }`.

Arguments:

- `channel` (required): integer, from 1 to 4
- `fit`: string, one of `cover`, `contain`
- `autoInclude`: boolean

#### `listDevices`

Lists the cameras and audio inputs the browser reports, with their device ids for setCameraSource and setAudioInput. Names can be empty until the person allows camera or microphone access.

Returns: `{ cameras: [{ deviceId, label }], audioInputs: [{ deviceId, label }] }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments: none.

#### `setCameraSource`

Shows a camera on a channel. `deviceId` picks a camera (see listDevices); empty or omitted is the default camera. The browser can ask the person for camera permission. `channel` defaults to the PVW channel.

Returns: `{ channel, source: "camera", deviceId }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments:

- `channel`: integer, from 1 to 4
- `deviceId`: string

### Switching

#### `setPreview`

Queues a channel on the PVW (preview) monitor.

Returns: `{ live, preview, transitioning }`.

Arguments:

- `channel` (required): integer, from 1 to 4

#### `take`

Takes a channel to program. Without `channel` it takes the PVW channel, and the outgoing program returns to PVW, like the TAKE (`cut`) and AUTO (`auto`) buttons. With `channel` it takes that channel and leaves PVW alone, like the program bus buttons. `auto` uses the selected transition type and time; `cut` switches at once, also during a transition. An `auto` take while a transition runs fails with CONFLICT_TRANSITION_RUNNING.

Returns: `{ live, preview, transitioning }`.

Arguments:

- `channel`: integer, from 1 to 4
- `transition`: string, one of `auto`, `cut`, default `auto`

#### `setTransition`

Sets the transition type (`cut`, `mix`, `wipe`), its time in seconds, the fade curve (also used by OUTPUT FADE) and the MIX blend mode. Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: `{ type, time, curve, blend }`.

Arguments:

- `type`: string, one of `cut`, `mix`, `wipe`
- `time`: number, from 0 to 4
- `curve`: string, one of `linear`, `dipped`, `sharp`, `cut`
- `blend`: string, one of `mix`, `add`, `screen`, `multiply`

#### `setAuto`

Sets beat-synced auto-switching: AUTO on or off, the mode (`scan`, `random`, `follows-audio`), bars per switch, the tempo in BPM, and SYNC (match the tempo to the audio). Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: `{ on, mode, bars, bpm, matchAudio }`.

Arguments:

- `on`: boolean
- `mode`: string, one of `scan`, `random`, `follows-audio`
- `bars`: integer, from 1 to 32
- `bpm`: number, from 40 to 300
- `matchAudio`: boolean

### Composition

#### `setComposition`

Sets the composition type (`off`, `pinp`, `split`, `quad`) and the PinP and SPLIT parameters. Positions run from -50 (left or top) through 0 (centre) to 50. Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: `{ mode, pinp, split }`.

Arguments:

- `mode`: string, one of `off`, `pinp`, `split`, `quad`
- `pinp`: object, with any of these fields
  - `source`: integer, from 1 to 4
  - `size`: string, one of `1/2`, `1/3`, `1/4`
  - `aspect`: string, one of `16:9`, `1:1`
  - `shape`: string, one of `square`, `diamond`, `circle`, `heart`
  - `borderWidth`: integer, from 0 to 15
  - `borderColor`: string, one of `black`, `white`, `gray`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `yellow`
  - `hPosition`: number, from -50 to 50
  - `vPosition`: number, from -50 to 50
  - `hCropping`: number, from 1 to 100
  - `vCropping`: number, from 1 to 100
  - `hViewPosition`: number, from -50 to 50
  - `vViewPosition`: number, from -50 to 50
- `split`: object, with any of these fields
  - `sourceB`: integer, from 1 to 4
  - `pattern`: string, one of `v-center`, `h-center`, `v-stretch`, `h-stretch`
  - `aCenter`: number, from 0 to 100
  - `bCenter`: number, from 0 to 100
  - `centerPosition`: number, from -50 to 50

#### `setKey`

Sets the KEY overlay: on or off, `chroma` or `luma`, its source (a channel, or `still`, which a Seance session cannot use), LEVEL and GAIN (0 to 255) and the key colour. Turning the key on with no source keys channel 1. Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: `{ on, type, source, level, gain, chromaColor, lumaColor }`, where `source` is a channel, `still` or `null`.

Arguments:

- `on`: boolean
- `type`: string, one of `chroma`, `luma`
- `source`: integer or string, one of `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `still`
- `level`: integer, from 0 to 255
- `gain`: integer, from 0 to 255
- `chromaColor`: string, one of `green`, `blue`
- `lumaColor`: string, one of `white`, `black`

### Output

#### `setOutput`

Sets FREEZE (hold the program frame), OUTPUT FADE (fade the program to black over the fade time) and the output VFX filter. Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: `{ freeze, fade, vfx }`, where `fade` is true while the output fades to or holds black.

Arguments:

- `freeze`: boolean
- `fade`: boolean
- `vfx`: string, one of `none`, `negative`, `mono`, `sepia`, `posterize`, `emboss`, `edges`

#### `captureStill`

Captures the program as a still, like the STILL button. The still becomes the KEY source `still` and the channel source `still`. HD4 also keeps its bytes in this browser, as the STILL button does, so memory slots can name it.

Returns: `{ captured, width, height }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments: none.

#### `setRecording`

Starts or stops recording the program and its audio. Stopping saves the recording as a browser download.

Returns: `{ recording }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments:

- `recording` (required): boolean

#### `openViewport`

Opens the program in a window for a secondary display, or focuses it. A pop-up blocker can refuse it.

Returns: `{ open }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments: none.

### Audio

#### `setAudioChannel`

Sets one channel strip: fader (0 to 1), mute, solo, its audio source (`follow` the video, or `none`) and its processing (`strip`: high-pass filter, 3-band EQ, gate, compressor, pan, delay, AUX and reverb sends, auto-audio). Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: `{ channel, fader, mute, solo, source }`.

Arguments:

- `channel` (required): integer, from 1 to 4
- `fader`: number, from 0 to 1
- `mute`: boolean
- `solo`: boolean
- `source`: string, one of `follow`, `none`
- `strip`: object, with any of these fields
  - `hpf`: boolean
  - `eqHi`: number, from -15 to 15
  - `eqHiFreq`: number, from 1000 to 20000
  - `eqMid`: number, from -15 to 15
  - `eqMidFreq`: number, from 20 to 20000
  - `eqMidQ`: number, from 0.5 to 16
  - `eqLo`: number, from -15 to 15
  - `eqLoFreq`: number, from 20 to 500
  - `gate`: boolean
  - `gateThreshold`: number, from -80 to 0
  - `gateAttack`: number, from 0.5 to 200
  - `gateRelease`: number, from 30 to 5000
  - `comp`: boolean
  - `compThreshold`: number, from -60 to 0
  - `compRatio`: number, from 1 to 100
  - `compAttack`: number, from 0.2 to 100
  - `compRelease`: number, from 30 to 5000
  - `compMakeup`: number, from -40 to 40
  - `compAutoGain`: boolean
  - `pan`: number, from -1 to 1
  - `delay`: number, from 0 to 500
  - `auxSend`: number, from -60 to 10
  - `revSend`: number, from -60 to 10
  - `followVideo`: boolean
  - `autoMixEnabled`: boolean
  - `autoMixWeight`: number, from 0 to 100

#### `setAudioMain`

Sets the main fader (0 to 1), what the speakers monitor (`main` or the `aux` mix), what a recording captures (`program` or `aux`), and the main bus (`bus`: mute, limiter, EQ, reverb, multiband compressor, AUX bus, AUTO MIXING). Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: `{ fader, monitor, recordSource }`.

Arguments:

- `fader`: number, from 0 to 1
- `monitor`: string, one of `main`, `aux`
- `recordSource`: string, one of `program`, `aux`
- `bus`: object, with any of these fields
  - `mainMute`: boolean
  - `mainLimiter`: boolean
  - `mainLimiterThreshold`: number, from -40 to 0
  - `eqHi`: number, from -15 to 15
  - `eqHiFreq`: number, from 1000 to 20000
  - `eqMid`: number, from -15 to 15
  - `eqMidFreq`: number, from 20 to 20000
  - `eqMidQ`: number, from 0.5 to 16
  - `eqLo`: number, from -15 to 15
  - `eqLoFreq`: number, from 20 to 500
  - `reverbReturn`: number, from -60 to 10
  - `reverbTime`: number, from 0 to 5
  - `reverbType`: string, one of `room`, `hall`
  - `mbComp`: boolean
  - `mbHiThres`: number, from -40 to 0
  - `mbMidThres`: number, from -40 to 0
  - `mbLoThres`: number, from -40 to 0
  - `mbHiRatio`: number, from 1 to 100
  - `mbMidRatio`: number, from 1 to 100
  - `mbLoRatio`: number, from 1 to 100
  - `auxMute`: boolean
  - `auxLevel`: number, from -60 to 10
  - `auxDelay`: number, from 0 to 500
  - `autoMixing`: boolean

#### `setAudioInput`

Uses an audio input device as a channel's audio source. `deviceId` empty or omitted is the default input. The browser can ask the person for microphone permission.

Returns: `{ channel, source }`, where `source` is `device`, or `none` when the input did not start.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments:

- `channel` (required): integer, from 1 to 4
- `deviceId`: string

### Memory

#### `listMemory`

Lists the eight memory slots, which this browser keeps.

Returns: `{ slots: [{ slot, occupied }] }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments: none.

#### `saveMemory`

Saves the full mixer state to a memory slot, replacing what the slot held. A slot keeps channel sources, fit, PVW, the program channel, transition, VFX, composition and audio.

Returns: `{ saved: true, slot }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments:

- `slot` (required): integer, from 1 to 8

#### `recallMemory`

Recalls a memory slot. A source that cannot start (a camera without permission) falls back on its channel.

Returns: `{ recalled: true, slot }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments:

- `slot` (required): integer, from 1 to 8

### Settings

#### `getSettings`

Returns the settings this browser keeps (output resolution, OUTPUT FADE time, SYNC beat sensitivity, theme), the USER button assignments and the actions a USER button can take.

Returns: `{ settings, userButtons: [{ button, action }], actions: [{ id, label }] }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments: none.

#### `setSettings`

Sets the program output resolution, the OUTPUT FADE time in seconds, the SYNC beat sensitivity and the theme. The settings persist in this browser. Omitted fields keep their value.

Returns: every setting.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments:

- `resolution`: string, one of `640x360`, `1280x720`, `1920x1080`
- `outputFadeTime`: number, from 0.1 to 3
- `beatSensitivity`: number, from 1 to 3
- `theme`: string, one of `neutral-dark`, `gray-dark`, `ocean`, `dusk`, `sunset`, `terminal`

#### `setUserButton`

Assigns an action to a USER button (1 to 5), or `none`. The assignment persists in this browser.

Returns: `{ button, action }`.

Through a Seance session: not available (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`). It needs the person at the browser, or it reads or changes what this browser keeps.

Arguments:

- `button` (required): integer, from 1 to 5
- `action` (required): string, one of `take:1`, `take:2`, `take:3`, `take:4`, `cut`, `mix`, `wipe`, `quad`, `pinp`, `split`, `key`, `freeze`, `fade`, `still`, `record`, `auto`, `mem:1`, `mem:2`, `mem:3`, `mem:4`, `mem:5`, `mem:6`, `mem:7`, `mem:8`, `none`

### Images

#### `getThumbnail`

Returns an image of the program output (`program`), of the PVW channel (`preview`) or of channel 1 to 4. Through a Seance session the image is added to the session as its own bytes, and `image` replaces `bytes`; there it answers REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE unless every channel shows a program (a channel still showing the last frame of its previous source counts as not showing it), the KEY does not show the still and FREEZE is off, because cameras, video, images and stills stay on the person's computer. The program output also answers it while the person's tab is hidden and does not draw it.

Returns: `{ bytes, mimeType, width, height, source, channel }`, with `bytes` in base64 and `channel` the channel shown (`null` for the program output). Through a session: `{ image: { id, mimeType, bytes }, mimeType, width, height, source, channel }`, where `image.bytes` is the byte count.

Arguments:

- `maxDimension`: integer, from 16 to 1024, default `256`
- `format`: string, one of `png`, `jpg`, default `jpg`
- `source`: string or integer, one of `program`, `preview`, `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, default `program`
